newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Offers flat in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Offers flat in quiet trade.

text.p: Rail and truck soymeal offers were unchanged on Wednesday, with most dealers reporting very little trade.
"I haven't sold more than a few truckloads all week," said one Indiana-based dealer.

Basis values and CBOT prices remained too high to attract much interest from end-users. One dealer said that CBOT futures need to drop $5.00 per ton to entice buyers and basis needs to fall $3.00 per ton, he said.
"If we saw those kinds of prices, I think we would see a lot of people come into the market," the dealer said.
Ongoing exports of soymeal continued to support basis levels, a Midwest dealer said.
One dealer in the northern Midwest said buying enthusiasm had been dampened by the upcoming U.S. federal and state tax season.
"This is tax time for a lot of people, so they aren't
going to buy a lot of stuff," the dealer said.
